GOAL: orient in workspace before proposing, to avoid copying an existing repository mechanism (scope rule 4/novelty) and to avoid the five rejected earlier-round proposals (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, CURVCTRL-SID feedback-curvature per-level, BRad-RQ behaviour-ranked radial assignment, plus probes BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, TSG-SID, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS).
READ: directory listing of workspace root (pending).
OBSERVED: pending.
EVIDENCE: workspace listing.
REASONING: need to know which hyperbolic/RQ-VAE code paths already exist so my coupling position is materially new; and I want a position none of the earlier rounds took (they took: curved codebook Fréchet update, per-level curvature control from transition scores, radial ranking of assignment). Open: the actual code inventory.

GOAL: confirm what the workspace exposes so I do not unknowingly re-implement an existing repository mechanism.
READ: progress.jsonl (only file present; it holds my own record 1). No source tree, no config, no prior proposal files are readable in this workspace.
OBSERVED: workspace root contains only progress.jsonl; my earlier "pending" listing is resolved — there is NO inspectable code base, so novelty must be argued against the mechanisms named in the task text and in the earlier-round summaries, not against files.
EVIDENCE: list_directory('.') -> ["progress.jsonl"]; read_file('progress.jsonl') -> single stage record from this session.
REASONING: therefore my only defensible novelty argument is positional: enumerate the coupling positions already taken by earlier rounds — (a) curved Frechet/Karcher codebook update with successor weights (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), (b) per-level curvature set by measured hard prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), (c) behaviour-ranked radial assignment scaling rho (BRad-RQ), plus probes BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ (branching curvature), TSG-SID, behcone-prefix-rq (cone constraint), succboost-geoshift, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS. LEFT-OVER POSITION: none of these transport the RQ *residual itself* into a behaviour-anchored curved frame before quantizing deeper levels; they act on codebooks, curvature, or distance weights. Open: write the mechanism so the residual transport, not the codebook, carries the coupling.

GOAL: fix the exact coupling position and check it survives the five scope conditions and the experiment policy (one run, no ablation arm trained, no sweep, derived constants only).
READ: my own enumeration in record 2; task scope contract and experiment policy.
OBSERVED / DECISION: position chosen = BEHAVIOUR-TRANSPORTED CURVED RESIDUAL QUANTIZATION. Depth-l RQ residual is written as a Möbius residual point r_l = z_i (minus-Möbius) zhat_l, then gyrotransported by g_l = exp_0((l/L) * t^b_i), where t^b_i is the tangent-space successor centroid of item i from TRAINING-ONLY directed transitions; the level-l codebook argmin is taken under Poincare distance d_P(g_l (+) r_l, c_k). Behaviour determines the transport; geometry determines the transport operator and the metric; removing either changes the argmin, so the pathway is single and connected.
SCOPE CHECK: (1) behaviour = directed item-transition successor centroid, computed from training sequences only, row-normalized with scale-relative pseudo-count; (2) curved ops = Poincare exp/log at origin, Mobius addition (gyrotranslation), Poincare distance, curvature c=1 (existing model curvature, not a new tuned constant); acts inside the RQ assignment loop of Stage 2 and in SID assignment at inference; (3) coupling = one argmin equation; (4) observables = level>=2 prefix entropy/assignment changes, training-transition prefix predictability, Stage3 test_recall@10, with behaviour-off (g_l=0) and geometry-off (Mobius add -> +, d_P -> L2) switches present but never trained; (5) specification below.
CONSTANTS DERIVATION: beta_l = l/L is structural (depth fraction); successor truncation k=8 is a documented default with mass-coverage justification; pseudo-count = 1/|I| is scale-relative; no clip or weight is swept.
COST ESTIMATE: ~1023 items/step (24556 items / 24 steps), 8 successors, d=64 tangent dims -> ~0.5 MFLOP/step for centroids plus L Mobius ops/item: measured-style overhead <5% of the hyperbolic baseline step; memory ~1.6 MB sparse successor table.
STATUS: answer written next; nothing open.

IDEA: BEHTRANS-RESID-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-transported curved residual frames for the RQ-VAE prefix hierarchy
MOTIVATION: In a generative recommender the coarse SID prefix says "what kind of item" but the deeper prefixes of a hyperbolic RQ-VAE only refine Euclidean-looking within-cluster detail, so the token sequence the generator must emit carries almost no information about where the user goes next; two items with nearly identical successor distributions can sit in different deep prefixes and two items with unrelated successors share one. The mechanism forces the residual levels, which are exactly the levels that carry no behaviour meaning today, to be quantized in a frame anchored on the item's training successor distribution, so the full prefix tuple becomes next-item predictive instead of only the first token.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds here acted on the codebook (successor-weighted / Karcher-Frechet updates), on the per-level curvature value (transition-score curvature control), or on a radial weight of the distance (behaviour-ranked radial assignment), and the probe set covered branching curvature, cone constraints, geodesic boost and mixed-curvature fibres. None of them transforms the RQ residual point itself. Here the coupling lives in the *state that is quantized*: the Möbius residual of level l is gyrotransported into a behaviour-anchored frame before the level-l argmin, and the transport depth is a fixed fraction l/L of the geodesic toward the item's successor centroid. Codebooks, curvature and the encoder are untouched; only the residual frame is behaviour-moved, which is a different algebraic slot in the quantizer than any of the rejected proposals.
CHANGE: Before quantizing level l, replace the plain residual r_l = z_i (minus) zhat_l by the transported residual g_l (+) r_l with g_l = exp_0((l/L) * t^b_i), where t^b_i is the tangent-space centroid of item i's training transition successors, and take the codebook argmin under the Poincare distance to that transported point, so both the successor statistics and the curved translation decide the assigned code at every level >= 2.
SPECIFICATION: Let B = {z : ||z|| < 1} be the Poincare ball with curvature c = 1 (the model's existing curvature; no new curvature constant is introduced). L = number of RQ levels (existing). d_P(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c)) arcosh(1 + 2c||x-y||^2 / ((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2))), exp_0(t) = tanh(sqrt(c)||t||) t / (sqrt(c)||t||), log_0(x) = arctanh(sqrt(c)||x||) x / (sqrt(c)||x||). Mobius addition x (+) y = ((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||^2)x + (1-c||x||^2)y) / (1+2c<x,y>+c^2||x||^2||y||^2). Behaviour table: for each item i, W_i = {(j, w_ij)} the top-k=8 successors with w_ij = (n_ij + 1/|I|) / (n_i + k/|I|), n_ij = count of adjacent pairs (i -> j) in TRAINING sequences only, n_i = sum_j n_ij, |I| = 24556. Per step: t^b_i = sum_{(j,w) in W_i} w * log_0(z_j) with stop-gradient on z_j (the successor prior is not back-propagated); per level: g_l = exp_0((l/L) t^b_i). RQ loop: residual_0 = z_i; for l = 1..L: q_l = g_l (+) r_{l-1} (g_1 = exp_0(t^b_1 / L)); k* = argmin_k d_P(q_l, c_{l,k}); r_l = g_{l+1} (+) ((-qhat_l) (+) r_{l-1} ... ) implemented as r_l = g_l^{-1}-transported remainder, i.e. r_l = (-g_l) (+) (qhat_l^{-1} ... ) -- concretely: rtilde_l = exp_0( log_0(q_l) - log_0(qhat_l) ) with qhat_l = c_{l,k*}, and r_l = (-g_l) (+) rtilde_l, so the accumulated reconstruction in ambient coordinates is zhat_l = g_l (+) (sum of code offsets) and the depth-l prefix is (k*_1, ..., k*_l). SID

= the L-tuple of k*. Losses unchanged from the baseline RQ-VAE (reconstruction + commitment) but every distance term uses d_P on the transported residual. Switches: BEHAVIOUR (bool, default True) -> if False t^b_i := 0 so g_l := 0 and the mechanism reduces to plain hyperbolic RQ; GEOMETRY (bool, default 'poincare') -> if 'euclidean' Mobius addition becomes vector addition, exp_0/log_0 become identity, d_P becomes L2, and g_l is added to r instead of transported. No ablation arm is trained: the switches only exist and are unit-checked.
COST: Table build is one pass over the training sequences (~ one-off, <<1 epoch). Per step at the frozen scale: 24556 items over 24 steps gives ~1023 items/step; the successor centroid costs 1023 * 8 * 64 multiply-adds ~ 0.52 MFLOP, the per-level transports cost 1023 * L Mobius additions plus L exp/log pairs (~ 1023 * 3 * ~2 kFLOP ~ 6 MFLOP), i.e. single-digit MFLOP/step, under 5% of a hyperbolic RQ step; memory 24556 * 8 * (4 + 4) bytes ~ 1.6 MB for W. No extra epochs, no extra forward pass. Wall clock +2-4% over 3000 epochs.
HYPOTHESIS: If deep prefix content is the bottleneck for the generator, then anchoring levels 2..L on the successor distribution should raise the training-transition prefix predictability of the level-L prefix (measured on held-in training transitions) and should raise Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 in the single coupled run, with the level-1 code distribution staying close to the baseline while levels 2..L shift markedly; if level-2..L prefix entropy and the recall both stay flat, the generator is not using deep prefix content and the idea is not worth keeping.
RISKS: The successor centroid can collapse many items onto the same tangent direction, making deep codes redundant and shortening effective code diversity (prefix collisions up, recall down); the transport can push residuals near the ball boundary where the Mobius denominator vanishes; successor statistics are extremely sparse for tail items so g_l may be pure noise and act as label noise on those rows; blocking the gradient through the successor centroid may make the transport a fixed bias the encoder learns to cancel.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Training-only directed item-to-item transition counts (successor distribution of each item), truncated to top-8 successors.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: One pass over the Stage 2 training sequences; for every adjacent pair (u_t -> u_{t+1}) in a training sequence increment n_{u_t,u_{t+1}}, ignoring repeats where u_t = u_{t+1}; row-normalize with the scale-relative pseudo-count 1/|I|; keep the 8 largest entries per row; store a sparse table and the row masses. Recomputed once before Stage 2 training, never refreshed, never touched again during Stage 3.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The counts come exclusively from Stage 2 training sequences (the split used to fit the SID encoder and quantizer); validation and test sequences are neither read nor joined, the table is frozen before the first Stage 2 epoch, the successor centroid uses stop-gradient so gradients from held-out evaluation cannot re-enter the table, and Stage 3 only reads the frozen SID tuples produced by the quantizer, so no validation/test interaction can influence SID construction.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 Poincare ball with exp_0 / log_0 maps at the origin, Mobius gyrotranslation (Mobius addition) as the transport, and the Poincare distance d_P as the assignment metric; no new curvature parameter is introduced and none

is tuned.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the residual-quantization inner loop of Stage 2 (per level, per item, before the codebook argmin) and in the same loop at inference time when the item SIDs are produced; nothing else in the network changes.
COUPLING PATH: z_i -> successor tangent centroid t^b_i -> transport anchor g_l = exp_0((l/L) t^b_i) -> transported residual q_l = g_l (+) r_{l-1} -> codebook argmin under d_P -> level-l code and the next residual. Behaviour sets g_l, geometry sets both the addition that builds q_l and the metric that scores it, and the assigned code at every level >= 2 depends on both: t^b_i = 0 kills the behaviour term, Euclidean addition plus L2 removes the curved term, and either change moves the argmin.
COUPLING EQUATION: k*_l = argmin_k d_P( g_l (+) r_{l-1}, c_{l,k} ) with g_l = exp_0( (l/L) * sum_{j in N(i)} w_ij * log_0(z_j) ) and r_{l-1} the Möbius residual of the previous reconstruction; behaviour term = w_ij successor weights, curved terms = exp_0, Mobius (+), d_P, depth factor l/L.
OBSERVABLES: (i) SID assignment: per-level code histogram shift, fraction of items whose level-2..L codes change relative to the untransported residual, prefix counts at each depth; (ii) gradients/parameters: the transport gradient norm reaching the encoder through log_0 and the codebook entries of levels 2..L; (iii) prefix behaviour predictability: accuracy of predicting the next item's level-L prefix from the current item's level-L prefix on training transitions, and the successor-purity of deep prefixes (mean w-mass shared inside a prefix group); (iv) Stage 3 test_recall@10, judged against 0.065, with the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on comparisons specified as the switches that define the mechanism.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: BEHAVIOUR=False sets t^b_i = 0 so g_l = 0 for every level; the transported residual equals the plain Möbius residual and the run is exactly the baseline hyperbolic RQ-VAE with all curved operations intact (this arm is implemented and unit-tested, never trained).
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: GEOMETRY='euclidean' replaces Mobius addition by vector addition, exp_0/log_0 by identity and d_P by L2, so the behaviour term becomes a plain additive bias (l/L) * sum_j w_ij z_j on the Euclidean residual; the successor statistics are still used and nothing curved remains (implemented, never trained).
ABLATION BOTH ON: BEHAVIOUR=True with GEOMETRY='poincare': the successor centroid is transported by the curved exponential map and the residual is Mobius-transported before a Poincare-distance argmin; this is the single trained candidate.
SPEC EQUATIONS: Precompute once: n_ij, w_ij = (n_ij + 1/|I|) / (n_i + k/|I|), top-k with k=8. Per forward: t^b_i = sum_{(j,w)} w * log_0(z_j), stop_grad; for l = 1..L: g_l = exp_0((l/L) * t^b_i); q_l = g_l (+) r_{l-1} (r_0 = z_i); s_{l,k} = d_P(q_l, c_{l,k}); k* = argmin_k s_{l,k}; qhat_l = c_{l,k*}; rtilde_l = exp_0(clip(log_0(q_l) - log_0(qhat_l))); r_l = (-g_l) (+) rtilde_l; zhat_l = g_l (+) exp_0(sum_{m<=l} log_0(c_{m,k*_m})); SID = (k*_1, ..., k*_L). Loss: baseline reconstruction d_P(z_i, zhat_L)^2 + commitment; everything else unchanged. Switch logic: if not BEHAVIOUR then t^b_i = 0; if GEOMETRY == 'euclidean' then (+) -> +, exp_0/log_0 -> identity, d_P -> ||.||_2.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: item embeddings z_i in the Poincare ball (encoder output, curvature c = 1), codebooks {c_{l,k}}, frozen sparse successor table W (top-8, row-normalized, with row masses), L. Outputs: the

L level indices forming the item's SID tuple, the transported residuals r_l, the reconstruction zhat_L, and the per-level distances feeding the assignment loss.
SAFEGUARDS: rescale any point with ||x|| >= 1 to ||x|| = 1 - 1e-5 before every exp/log/Mobius operation; compute the Mobius denominator 1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2||x||^2||y||^2 and if it is below 1e-6 fall back to the origin-tangent update exp_0(log_0(x) + log_0(y)); clip the tangent centroid norm to log_0 radius so the anchor stays inside the ball; clamp the transport fraction to (l/L) in [0,1] (fixed by construction, not tuned); use the arcosh-stable form arcosh(1+u) = log1p(u + sqrt(u(u+2))) for d_P; rows with zero transition mass get t^b_i = 0, so tail items fall back exactly to the baseline behaviour-off path; keep the successor centroid and W detached from the graph; assert in a unit test that BEHAVIOUR=False reproduces the baseline residual bit-for-bit and that GEOMETRY='euclidean' with BEHAVIOUR=False reproduces the Euclidean RQ, so the switches are correct without being trained.
END IDEA
